title: Squaring a bracket
hint: Careful: $(a + b)^2$ is not $a^2 + b^2$. Write it as $(a + b)(a + b)$ and multiply out: you get a middle term $2ab$ too.

title: Minus in front of a bracket
hint: The minus sign in front of the bracket changes the sign of EVERY term inside, not only the first one: $-(b - c + d) = -b + c - d$.

title: Cancelling terms
hint: You can only cancel factors (things multiplied), not terms (things added). In $\frac{x + 3}{x}$ the x on top is added to 3, so it cannot cancel.

title: Reversing the inequality
hint: When you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, you must reverse the inequality sign: $-2x > 6$ gives $x < -3$.

title: Multiplying by an unknown sign
hint: Do not multiply both sides by an expression like $(x - 2)$ when you do not know if it is positive or negative. Use a sign diagram instead.

title: Order of operations
hint: Multiply before you add or subtract. Work out the multiplication first, then do the subtraction.

title: Two minus signs
hint: Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding: $5 - (-6) = 5 + 6$.

title: Adding fractions
hint: Do not add the bottoms. First give both fractions the same denominator, then add the tops only.

title: Missing middle term
hint: Each term in the first bracket multiplies each term in the second. You should have four products, then collect the two x terms.

title: Signs in the brackets
hint: Check your signs by expanding your answer. The two numbers must multiply to the constant term AND add to the x coefficient, with the right signs.

title: Multiplying powers
hint: When you multiply powers of the same letter, add the powers: $x^3 \times x^4 = x^7$, not $x^{12}$.

title: Power of a product
hint: The power applies to everything inside the bracket, the number too: $(3x^2)^2 = 9x^4$.

title: Squaring a negative number
hint: A negative number squared is positive: $(-3)^2 = 9$. Use brackets when you substitute a negative number.

title: Order when rearranging
hint: Undo the operations in reverse order. If x was multiplied and then had a number added, first subtract the number, then divide.

title: Degree is not the number of terms
hint: The degree is the highest power of x, not how many terms there are.

title: Leading coefficient
hint: The leading coefficient belongs to the highest power of x, wherever it is written. Rewrite the polynomial with the powers in descending order first.

title: Subtracting in long division
hint: When you subtract a line in long division, subtract EVERY term: $(2x^2 - 7x) - (2x^2 - 4x) = -3x$. A minus sign in front of a negative gives a plus.

title: The sign in (x + a)
hint: For the divisor $(x + a)$, the remainder is $f(-a)$, not $f(a)$. Find the x that makes the divisor zero: $x + a = 0$ gives $x = -a$.

title: Dividing by (ax − b)
hint: For the divisor $(ax - b)$, use $x = \frac{b}{a}$: the value that makes $ax - b = 0$. For $(2x - 1)$, use $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$.
